completed_tasks.name: OFF-ROADMAP — launch engines outside DMM's own cgroup
completed_tasks.note: Written 2026-08-18, committed 2026-08-20. _launch_argv wraps bare-metal launches in `systemd-run --user --scope`; all 12 generated vLLM profiles moved from `exec docker run` to `docker run -d`. Root cause: DMM is a systemd --user unit, so Popen children inherited its cgroup and KillMode=control-group took them down on restart — a routine restart on 2026-08-18 stopped a vllm_node that had served 25 hours. start_new_session=True does not help (session != cgroup).

open_questions.q: Qwen3.8 dense (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration) emits no reasoning parser
open_questions.detail: model_capabilities.json now has the architecture as a match key at confidence template-inferred / emit=false. That RECORDS the gap; it does not close it. Without --reasoning-parser qwen3 a thinking model returns content=None and callers silently degrade. emit=true is not permitted: the 3.8 dense chat_template sha256 (12827f24) differs from the recipe-proven Qwen3.6 row (e84f32a2), and the known 3.8 repos disagree with each other (philbert440: c3cf9e34). Upgrading to recipe-proven requires a dense 3.8 actually serving under vLLM here — philbert440/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-Aggressive-NVFP4 is the cheap route at ~26 GB versus the bf16 base at ~87 GB.

open_questions.q: FastMTP needs the fork — settled, but the image does not exist
open_questions.detail: TESTED 2026-08-20: SPEC=fastmtp on stock upstream 555881e dies with `check_tensor_dims: tensor 'output.weight' has wrong shape; expected 5120, 248320, got 5120, 32768`. Upstream has the draft-mtp mechanism but rejects the sidecar's 32K-vocab output head. RECIPE=fast therefore fails on the missing fastmtp_image, which is correct — it fails before weights load. Building that image is optional future work; claimed gain is ~1.35x.

HauhauCS ships Ed25519 signatures and SHA256SUMS, all of which VERIFY on the local copy (manifest signature good; sidecar sha256 115e618e matches; pubkey DER f7be4a23 matches the provenance). But the public key ships in the same repo it signs, so the chain is circular — it proves integrity, not identity. philbert440 (Phil Tompkins, individual account) ships documented method and eval gates but no checksums. Neither is institutionally trusted. Treat both as untrusted artifacts.

Unlike vLLM, which has vllm-default-model.service owning post-reboot state, nothing restarts the llama.cpp container on failure or reboot. It deliberately carries no --restart policy (a policy on a possibly-wrong launch caused the 2026-08-04 outage), so the fix is a unit or a boot recipe, not a docker flag.

litellm's real source of truth is ~/dgx-stack/litellm-config-prod.yaml, NOT the ConfigMap. DMM's _sync_litellm runs `kubectl create configmap --from-file` against it on every profile switch, so ConfigMap edits are temporary. This is exactly how the 24-vs-1 drift arose.
Present timings in America/Chicago; the box and all crons are UTC.

GB10 is a noisy benchmark host — vLLM + k3s make single-run timings vary up to 7x. Use medians over >=5 reps for any perf claim. The 8.3 tok/s figure in task 12 is 3 reps and was used only to separate 'real kernels' from 'a 100x fallback', not as a benchmark.
